https://atomicdata.dev/properties/descri: The store's plugin gate: which of the bundled integrations in this folder are shown to every visitor of the Integrations page, and which stay hidden until a visitor enables 'Show experimental plugins'. Also owns the card copy for the bundled ones (`browser/data-browser/src/chunks/PluginRuns/IntegrationDiscovery.tsx` only keeps the one field JSON can't hold: a live reference to a LocalThought extension module). `shortname` on each PluginCatalogEntry matches a `BundledIntegration.id`. `enabled: false`, same as an id with no entry at all, makes it dark matter: its module is still compiled into the server as a static asset, but it is never offered, even with 'Show experimental plugins' on. Flip `experimental` to `false` once its package.json `atomicCertification.support` has left "experimental" — see integrations/README.md. This file is served as a static asset at `/integrations/catalog.json`; the data-browser fetches it from the connected server at runtime rather than bundling it at build time.
One integration's visibility gate and, for a bundled one, its card copy.

True until this integration's advertised capabilities have current live evidence. An experimental entry is hidden from the Integrations page unless the visitor turns on 'Show experimental plugins'. Only meaningful when `enabled` is true.

Whether this integration can be reached at all. False, same as omitting the entry entirely, makes it dark matter: its module is still compiled into the server as a static asset, but the Integrations page never offers it, even with 'Show experimental plugins' on.
What this bundled integration's sync or import can actually do, shown on its Integrations page card.

The supported scope and caveats, shown in the card's 'Supported scope' details.

True if this integration's card only appears once a visitor also enables 'Show API plugins', on top of any `experimental` gating.
